notes.3: The building was revalued upwards to $480 000 and, in theory had a further 32 years to be depreciated. The annual depreciation charge should, therefore have been $15 000. Most candidates divided $480 000 by 40 years, and used a depreciation figure of $12 000. Using this figure would mean that the building would not have been fully depreciated by year 40. The key was B, $480 000 – (2 × $15 000) = $450 000.

notes.30: This required consideration of budgeting. The key was D. The majority of candidates opted for C. However, it is not necessarily true that a budget is always prepared for a period of one year ahead. Consider, for instance, a possible cash budget required by the bank manager for the next six months.
